In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah Ibrahim

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book We have sent down to you, that you may bring mankind out of darkness into light by the permission of their Lord﴾ – the verse.

In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, makes clear that He sent down this great Book to His Prophet ﷺ so that through it he might bring people out of the darkness of disbelief and misguidance into the light of faith and guidance. He clarified this meaning in other verses,

• such as His saying: ﴿He it is who sends down to His servant clear signs that He may bring you out of darkness into light﴾ – the verse [al-Hadid: 9],

• and His saying: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out of darkness into light﴾ – the verse [al-Baqarah: 257], along with other verses, as the indication to this was previously given. Here He has also made clear that He does not bring anyone out of darkness into light except by His permission, may He be glorified and exalted, in His saying: ﴿by the permission of their Lord﴾ – the verse [Ibrahim: 1]. He clarified this in other verses,

• such as His saying: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by the permission of Allah﴾ – the verse [al-Nisa: 64],

• and His saying: ﴿And it is not for a soul to believe except by the permission of Allah﴾ – the verse [Yunus: 100],

along with other verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 4:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people, so that he might make clear to them. Then Allah leads astray whom He wills﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted makes clear that He did not send any messenger except with the language (lughah) of his people, because He sent no messenger except to his own people and not to others. However, He has made clear in other places that our Prophet ﷺ was sent to all of creation, without being restricted to his own people or to others,

such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158];

and His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1];

and His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾ [Saba': 28], and other verses that indicate the generality of his message to the people of every language. So he ﷺ is obligated to convey to the people of every language. We have already mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "Indeed, Allah favored Muhammad ﷺ over the prophets and over the people of the heavens." They said: "In what way, O Ibn 'Abbas, did He favor him over the people of the heavens?" He said: "Indeed Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And whoever among them says, 'Indeed, I am a god besides Him,' then We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Anbiya': 29]. And He said to Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, We have given you a clear conquest, that Allah may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will follow﴾ [al-Fath: 1, 2]." They said: "Then what is his favor over the prophets?" He said: "Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people, so that he might make clear to them﴾ [Ibrahim: 4], and Allah, mighty and majestic, said to Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾ [Saba': 28]. So He sent him to the jinn and mankind."

Abu Muhammad al-Darimi mentioned it in his "Musnad" as previously stated, and it is an explanation from Ibn 'Abbas of the verse in the manner we have mentioned. And knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 9:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But they put their hands over their mouths﴾ — the verse.

The scholars differed regarding the meaning of this noble verse. Some scholars said its meaning is that those disbelievers put the hands of their own selves into their mouths, biting them out of rage and fury at what the messengers had brought, since it involved deriding their intellects and reviling their idols. Among those who held this view were ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) chose it and cited as evidence His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they are alone, they bite their fingertips at you out of rage﴾ — the verse [Al ʿImran: 119]. This meaning is well known in the speech of the Arabs, and from it is the saying of the poet:

﻿"You return into his mouth the rancor of the envious, until he bites upon the palms."

That is, they enrage the envious until he bites his fingers and palms. Al-Qurtubi said: From it is also the saying of another:

"His hardship has consumed his fingertips, so he has come to bite upon me the ankle-bone."

That is, it has consumed his fingertips by biting. And the rajiz said:

"If Salma had seen my emaciation, and the thinness of my shin-bone and my hand,
and the distance of my family and the harshness of my lodging, she would have bitten the fingertips of her hand out of longing."

There are other opinions regarding the noble verse besides this. Among them: that when they heard the Book of Allah, they were amazed and returned their hands to their mouths in wonder. This is related from Ibn ʿAbbas. Among them: that when their prophet said to them, "I am the Messenger of Allah to you," they pointed with their fingers to their mouths, meaning "be silent," rejecting him and dismissing his words. This is related from Abu Salih. Among them: that the meaning of the verse is that they returned the words of the messengers and denied them with their mouths; the first pronoun then refers to the messengers and the second to the disbelievers, and in this view "fi" (in) is in the sense of "bi" (with). This view is related from Mujahid, Qatadah, and Muhammad ibn Ka'b. Ibn Jarir said: Its justification is that "fi" here means "bi," and it has been heard from the Arabs: "Allah admitted you into the Paradise (bi-al-Jannah)," meaning "into the Paradise." And the poet said:

"And I would desire them away from Luqayt and his kin, but as for Sunbus, I do not desire."

He means: "and I would desire them (bi-ha)." Ibn Kathir said: This view is supported by the explanation of the verse by its continuation, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they said: Indeed we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and indeed we are in grave doubt about that to which you invite us﴾ [Ibrahim: 9].

The one who narrates this, may Allah pardon him, says: The apparent meaning to me is contrary to what Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, inclined to; because coordination by "wa" (and) requires that what follows be different from what precedes it, which indicates that the intended meaning of His saying ﴿they put their hands﴾ — the verse — is other than the explicit statement of denial with their mouths. And Allah knows best. It has also been said: The meaning is that the disbelievers put their hands into the mouths of the messengers, rejecting what they said; in that case the first pronoun refers to the disbelievers and the second to the messengers. This is related from al-Hasan. It has been said: the disbelievers placed the hands of the messengers over the mouths of the messengers to silence them and cut off their speech; this is related from Muqatil. It has been said: the messengers returned the hands of the disbelievers into their mouths. Other views have also been said. You have seen the opinions and what the Qur'an testifies to among them, and Allah knows best.

Note

The broken plural of "fam" (mouth) as "afwah" indicates that its original form was "fuh," so the fa' and the waw were dropped and the mim was given in compensation for them.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed we have disbelieved in that with which you have been sent, and indeed we are in grave doubt about that to which you invite us.﴾

In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, stated explicitly that the disbelievers declared to the messengers that they disbelieve in them, and that they are in doubt about the revelation they brought. He, exalted is He, also specified some of them by name as having declared their disbelief in it and their doubt about what they were invited to, such as the statement of the people of Salih to him: ﴿Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped? And indeed we are in grave doubt about that to which you invite us﴾ [Hud: 62]. They also declared disbelief in it in His saying: ﴿The eminent ones of his people who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed, to those among them who believed: Do you know that Salih is sent from his Lord? They said: Indeed we believe in that with which he has been sent.﴾ ﴿Those who were arrogant said: Indeed we disbelieve in that which you have believed﴾ [Al-A'raf: 75], and similar verses. We have already mentioned, in the introduction to this blessed book, that among the kinds of exposition it contains is that it mentions a general statement in one verse, then explicitly includes some individual members of that generality in another verse, as here, and as the example was given earlier in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That, and whoever honors the rites of Allah﴾ [Al-Hajj: 32], along with His saying: ﴿And the camels We have made for you among the rites of Allah﴾ — the verse [Al-Hajj: 36].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 13:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, "We will surely expel you from our land, or you will return to our religion."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted has made clear that the disbelievers threatened the messengers with expulsion from their land and banishment from among them, if they did not abandon what they had brought of revelation (wahy). He has also stated in other verses some of this in detail:

• Such as His words concerning the people of Shu'ayb: ﴿O Shu'ayb, we will surely expel you and those who believed with you from our town, or you will return to our religion." He said, "Even though we are averse?"﴾ ﴿"We would have invented a lie against Allah if we returned to your religion..."﴾ to the end of the verse [al-A'raf: 88, 89],

• And His words concerning the people of Lut: ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel the family of Lut from your town. Indeed, they are men who keep themselves pure."﴾ [al-Naml: 56],

• And His words concerning the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿And indeed, they were about to unsettle you from the land to expel you from it; and then they would not remain after you, except for a little.﴾ [al-Isra': 76],

• And His words: ﴿And [recall] when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to restrain you or kill you or expel you. They plot, and Allah plots. And Allah is the best of planners.﴾ [al-Anfal: 30]

and other verses besides these.

* *

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So their Lord revealed to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers."﴾ ﴿"And We will surely settle you in the land after them. This is for whoever fears My standing and fears My threat."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted has made clear that He revealed to His messengers that the final outcome and victory belong to them over their enemies, and that He will settle them in the land after destroying their enemies. He has explained this meaning in many verses,

• such as His words: ﴿And We had already preceded Our word to Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers – they would be the predominant.﴾ [al-Saffat: 171–173],

• and His words: ﴿Allah has decreed, "I will surely prevail, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21],

• and His words: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believed in the worldly life.﴾ to the end of the verse [Ghafir: 51].

And His words: ﴿Moses said to his people, "Seek help in Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He causes to inherit it whom He wills of His servants. And the good outcome is for the righteous."﴾ [al-A'raf: 128], and His words: ﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed.﴾ to the end of the verse [al-A'raf: 137], and other verses besides these.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And every obstinate tyrant will be disappointed.﴾

Here He did not explain the manner of the disappointment of the obstinate tyrant, but He pointed to the meaning of his disappointment and some of his ugly attributes in His words in Surat Qaf: ﴿Cast into Hell every stubborn disbeliever, [who] forbids good, transgresses, [and is] in doubt, [and] who has set up with Allah another deity, so cast him into the severe punishment.﴾ (p-245) [Qaf: 24-25]. The jabbar (tyrant) is the one who is arrogant within himself, and the 'anid (obstinate) is the one who opposes the truth; this is what Ibn Kathir said.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 16:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Behind him is Hell﴾, and the verse.

"Warā'" (وراء) here means "in front of" (أمام), as is evident. This is supported by the use of "warā'" in the sense of "in front of" in the Qur'an and in Arabic speech. From the Qur'an is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And there was behind them a king who seized every boat by force﴾ [al-Kahf: 79], meaning: in front of them there was a king. Ibn 'Abbas used to recite it: "And there was in front of them a king who seized every boat by force." From the use of "warā'" in the sense of "in front of" in Arabic speech is the saying of Labid:

Is it not in front of me, if my death is delayed, the staff that the fingers bend over?

And the saying of another:

Do the Banu Marwan hope for my hearing and my obedience,
while my people, Tamim, and the wilderness are in front of me?

And his other saying:

And in front of you is a day you will reach,
no one present can escape it, and no one who goes out (to the desert) either.

So "warā'" in the verses means "in front of." Some scholars said the meaning of ﴿Behind him is Hell﴾ is: after his destruction, Hell (awaits him). Accordingly, "warā'" in the verse means "after." From the use of "warā'" in the sense of "after" is the saying of al-Nabigha:

I swore, and I did not leave for you any doubt,
and there is nothing after God for a man to go to.

That is: there is no refuge after God. This was said by al-Qurtubi. The first (meaning) is the apparent one and it is the truth.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 17:

The author said in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book):

[p. 315]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Ibrahim

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And death will come to him from every place﴾, and so on.

From its apparent meaning, one understands the death of the disbeliever in the Fire. His saying, ﴿and he is not dying﴾ [Ibrahim: 17], explicitly negates that.

The answer is that the meaning of ﴿and death will come to him﴾ is that its causes which normally necessitate it will come to him, except that Allah holds back his soul in his body while the factors that normally necessitate his death are present. Some later scholars, whose argument is not authoritative, clarified this meaning by saying:

*"I have killed you with satire, yet you did not die; indeed, dogs have long lives."*

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers, so can you relieve us of any portion of the punishment of Allah?"﴾

The argument that Allah mentions here about the disbelievers He explains in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And [mention] when they argue together in the Fire, and the weak say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed, we were your followers, so can you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?" Those who were arrogant will say, "Indeed, all of us are in it. Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants."﴾ [Ghafir: 47, 48], as its clarification has already been presented.

(p-247) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you.﴾

In this verse He made clear that Allah promised them the promise of truth, and that Satan promised them and then failed them in what he promised. He made this meaning clear in many verses:

• As His saying about Allah's promise: ﴿The promise of Allah is true﴾ [An-Nisa: 122],

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not fail in the appointment﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 31],

• and His saying about Satan's promise: ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires, but Satan promises them nothing except delusion﴾ [An-Nisa: 120]. And similar to these verses is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Their greeting therein will be peace﴾ [Ibrahim: 23].

In this noble verse He made clear that the greeting of the people of Paradise in Paradise is peace, and He made clear in other places that the angels greet them with it, and that some of them greet one another with it. So He said regarding the angels' greeting to them: ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, [saying]: Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 23-24]. He said: ﴿And its keepers will say to them: Peace be upon you; you have done well﴾ [Az-Zumar: 73]. He said: ﴿And they will be met therein with greeting and peace﴾ [Al-Furqan: 75]. And regarding their greeting to one another He said: ﴿Their call therein will be: Glory be to You, O Allah; and their greeting therein will be: Peace﴾ [Yunus: 10], as its explanation has already passed.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire."﴾

This is a threat from Him, exalted is He, to them that their destination is the Fire, and that brief enjoyment in this world does not benefit them against their destination to the Fire. He clarified this meaning in many verses,

• such as His saying: ﴿Say, "Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 8],

• and His saying: ﴿We give them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a severe punishment.﴾ [Luqman: 24],

• and His saying: ﴿[It is] an enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾ [Yunus: 70],

• and His saying: ﴿Let not the back-and-forth movement of those who disbelieve throughout the land deceive you. [It is but] a brief enjoyment; then their refuge is Hell﴾ and the verse [Ali 'Imran: 196, 197],

among other verses to that effect.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 31:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say to My servants who have believed: establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, before there comes a Day in which there is no trade and no close friendship.﴾

In this noble verse, the Exalted commands hastening to acts of obedience, such as the prayers and the charities, before the coming of the Day of Resurrection, which is the Day in which there is no trade and no close friendship (*khullah*, meaning intimate friendship) between two intimate friends. Then one of them does not benefit from the friendship of the other. No one can ransom himself by having his soul bought for him, and no friend benefits his friend on that Day. He explained this meaning in many verses,

such as His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided for you before there comes a Day in which there is no trade, no close friendship, and no intercession﴾ (2:254),

and His saying: ﴿So today no ransom will be taken from you or from those who disbelieved﴾ (57:15),

and His saying: ﴿And fear a Day when no soul will avail another soul at all﴾ (2:48),

and what is similar to that among the verses.

As for *khilal* (خِلال) in this verse, it has been said that it is the plural of *khullah* (خُلَّة), like *qullah* and *qilal*, and *khullah* means friendship. It has also been said that it is the verbal noun of *khallahu* (خالَّهُ) on the pattern of *fā'ala* (فاعَلَ), with the verbal nouns *mukhallah* (مُخالَّة) and *khilal* (خِلالًا). It is known that the verbal nouns of *fā'ala* are regularly formed on the patterns *mufā'alah* (المُفاعَلَة) and *fi'āl* (الفِعالَ). This is the apparent meaning. From it is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*I turned desire away from them out of fear of destruction, and I am not one who is hated in friendship, nor one who forsakes it.*

That is, I am not one whose friendship is disliked.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 35:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols﴾ — the verse.

He does not clarify here whether He answered this supplication of His Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), but He clarified in other places that He answered it for some of his offspring and not others, as in His saying: ﴿And among their offspring are one who does good and one who clearly wrongs himself﴾ [al-Saffat: 113], and His saying: ﴿And He made it a word lasting among his descendants﴾ — the verse [al-Zukhruf: 28].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾ — the verse.

In this noble verse, Allah, may He be exalted, explains that His Prophet Ibrahim said: indeed whoever follows him is of him, and that he referred the matter of whoever does not follow him to the will of Allah, may He be exalted: if Allah wills, He will forgive him, for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. He mentioned something similar concerning Isa son of Maryam in His saying: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 118]. He also mentioned concerning Nuh and Musa their harshness in supplication against their peoples. Of Nuh He said that he said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant﴾ up to His saying: ﴿a wicked disbeliever﴾ [Nuh: 26, 27]. And of Musa He said that he said: ﴿Our Lord, they have led astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 88]. The apparent meaning is that Nuh and Musa, peace be upon them and upon our Prophet, did not make that supplication against their peoples except after they knew from Allah that they were wretched in Allah's knowledge and would never believe. As for Nuh, Allah, may He be exalted, clearly told him this in His saying:

﴿And it was revealed to Nuh that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36]. As for Musa, he understood that from the words of his people to him: ﴿Whatever sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we will not be believers in you﴾ [al-A'raf: 132], for they said this statement after witnessing those great signs mentioned in al-A'raf and elsewhere.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So make hearts among the people incline towards them and provide for them from the fruits﴾ – the verse.

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, makes clear that His Prophet Ibrahim (peace and blessings be upon him and upon our Prophet) supplicated for his offspring, whom He had settled in the sacred city of Makkah, that Allah would provide them with fruits. (p-249) In Surat al-Baqarah He made clear that Ibrahim restricted this supplication to the believers among them, and that Allah informed him that He provides for all of them, believers and disbelievers alike, and that on the Day of Resurrection He punishes the disbeliever. This is by His saying: ﴿And when Ibrahim said: "My Lord, make this a secure city and provide its people with fruits, such of them as believe in Allah and the Last Day." He said: "As for him who disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little, then I will drive him to the punishment of the Fire, and wretched is the destination"﴾ – the verse [al-Baqarah: 126].

Some scholars said: the reason Ibrahim restricted the believers in this supplication for provision is that he first supplicated that Allah make his offspring imams (leaders), and he did not restrict it to the believers. So Allah informed him that the wrongdoers among his offspring do not deserve that. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when Ibrahim was tested by his Lord with certain words, and he fulfilled them, He said: "Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people." He said: "And from my descendants?" He said: "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124]. So when he wanted to supplicate for them for provision, he restricted the believers on account of that, saying: "and provide its people with fruits, such of them as believe in Allah and the Last Day." Then Allah informed him that provision is not like leadership: Allah provides for the disbeliever in this world but does not make him an imam. Therefore He said to him, regarding the request for leadership: "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers." And when he restricted the believers in seeking provision, He said to him: ﴿And as for him who disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little﴾ – the verse [al-Baqarah: 126].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 41:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Our Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾ – the verse.

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, makes clear that Ibrahim (Abraham) asked for forgiveness for his parents. And He makes clear in other verses that his seeking forgiveness for his father was only before he knew that he was an enemy of Allah; when he knew that, he disassociated himself from him, as in His saying: ﴿And the plea of forgiveness by Ibrahim for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy to Allah, he disassociated himself from him﴾ [at-Tawbah: 114], and similar verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 42:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He only defers them to a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾.

In this noble verse, Exalted is He clarifies that He defers the punishment of the disbelievers until a Day on which eyes will stare fixedly from the intensity of fear. He made this clear in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the true promise draws near, and behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly﴾ [al-Anbiya': 97], and the meaning of the staring of the eyes (shukhus al-absar) is that they remain wide open, not closing, from the terror and the intensity of fear.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 43:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Hastening forward﴾.

Al-Ihţā' (hastening, rushing) in the language means al-Is'ā' (speeding, hurrying). Allah the Exalted has made clear in other places that on the Day of Resurrection they will come "hastening" (muhţi'īn), i.e., rushing when they are summoned to the reckoning,

• such as His saying: ﴿They will emerge from the graves as if they were scattered locusts, hastening toward the caller﴾ [al-Qamar: 7],

• and His saying: ﴿On the day they emerge from the graves in haste, as if they were rushing toward a idol-stone they are racing to reach﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 43],

• and His saying: ﴿On the day the earth splits asunder from them, hastening. That is a gathering that is easy for Us﴾ [Qaf: 44],

and other verses besides these.

And from the use of al-Ihţā' in the language in the sense of al-Is'ā' is the poet's saying:

Their home was in Dijlah, and indeed I saw them in Dijlah hastening toward the sound (of singing).

That is, rushing toward it.

The author said in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the day the earth will be changed into a different earth﴾ – the verse.

This noble verse explicitly states the changing of the earth on the Day of Resurrection. In another verse there appears something from which one may imagine that the earth will remain and not change. It is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed. And indeed, We will make what is upon it a barren wasteland﴾ [al-Kahf: 7–8]. In this verse He, exalted is He, explicitly states that He made what is on the earth an adornment for it in order to test creation. Then He explained that He will make what is upon it a barren wasteland, but He did not mention that He will change the earth itself. So one may imagine that the change occurs only in what is on it, not in the earth itself.

The answer is that the wisdom in mentioning what is on it rather than the earth itself is that what is on the earth of adornments, embellishments and the goods of this world is the cause of temptation, transgression, and disobedience to Allah, exalted is He.

So the report that it is perishable and transient contains the greatest admonisher and the most mighty restrainer from being seduced by it. For this wisdom it was singled out for mention. Therefore it does not contradict the change of the earth explicitly stated in the other verse, as is (p-316) evident. Moreover, the implication of His saying ﴿what is upon it﴾ is a *mafhum al-laqab* (an implication drawn from a named subject, i.e., a designation by name), since the relative pronoun refers to all the kinds that exist upon the earth as adornment for it. The implication of *mafhum al-laqab* is not considered by the majority of scholars (al-Jumhur). If it is not considered, then no contradiction appears at all. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 49:

Allah says: ﴿And you will see the criminals that Day bound together in shackles.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah explains that the criminals, who are the disbelievers, will be bound together in shackles on the Day of Resurrection. Allah explains this meaning in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And when they are thrown into a narrow place within it, bound together, they will call out there for destruction.﴾ [al-Furqan: 13], and similar verses.

Al-asfad (shackles, fetters) are the chains and bonds; its singular is ṣafd, with a sukun on the fa', and ṣafad, with a fatha on the fa'. From it is the saying of 'Amr ibn Kulthum:

They returned with plunder and captives, and we returned with kings bound in chains.

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver, and others bound together in shackles﴾ [Sad: 37, 38].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 50:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Fire will cover their faces﴾.

In this noble verse He makes clear that on the Day of Resurrection the Fire will cover the faces of the disbelievers and burn them, and He explains this in other places, such as His saying: ﴿The Fire will scorch their faces, and they therein will be grimacing﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 104], and His saying: ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to avert the Fire from their faces or from their backs﴾ [al-Anbiya': 39], and other verses besides these.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 14, verse 52:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿This is a message (balagh) for mankind﴾.

In this noble verse He makes clear that this Qur'an is a message for all of mankind. He clarified this meaning in His saying: ﴿And this Qur'an was revealed to me that I may warn you thereby, and whomever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19]. He also made clear that whoever it reaches and does not believe in it will be in the Fire, whoever he may be, in His saying: ﴿But whoever of the factions disbelieves in it, then the Fire is his promised place. So do not be in doubt about it﴾ [Hud: 17], and the rest of the verse.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And that they may know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may be reminded﴾.

In this noble verse He makes clear that among the wisdoms of sending down the great Qur'an is the knowledge that He, may He be exalted, is one God, and that among its wisdoms is that people of intellect may take heed. He explained this in other places. He mentioned the first wisdom at the beginning of Surah Hud in His saying: ﴿A Book whose verses are made firm and then detailed from One who is All-Wise and All-Aware, [saying]: Worship none but Allah﴾ [Hud: 1, 2], as its explanation has already passed. He mentioned the second wisdom in His saying: ﴿A Book which We have revealed to you, blessed, that they may reflect upon its verses and that those of understanding may be reminded﴾ [Sad: 29]. (p-251) They are the people of sound intellects, free from defects of deficiency. The singular of "al-albab" is "lubb" (with a dammah), and knowledge rests with Allah, may He be exalted.
